title: Factorise the Quadratic
text:
For $x^2 + x - 6$:
- Product = -6
- Sum = 1

Numbers: 3 and -2 (since $3 \times (-2) = -6$ and $3 + (-2) = 1$)

So: $x^2 + x - 6 = (x + 3)(x - 2)$

title: Complete Factorisation
text:
$x^3 - 7x + 6 = (x - 1)(x + 3)(x - 2)$

Set each factor equal to zero:
- $x - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 1$
- $x + 3 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -3$
- $x - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2$

title: Final Answer
text:
The solutions are $x = -3$, $x = 1$, and $x = 2$.

Note: This cubic actually has three distinct roots, not a repeated root as initially suggested. Verify: the problem statement may have intended a different polynomial.
